title: Extended Care Health Option (ECHO) End of Registration
content:
An Extended Care Health Option (ECHO) registration ends under the registration end rule when DEERS shows the sponsor separated or retired (after the continuation months after sponsor retirement), when the transitional survivor period ends, or when the case manager finds the qualifying condition no longer present at recertification every recertification interval in months. A family may end the registration at any time, but only by its own confirmation recorded on an intake. Services after the end date are not paid.

The registration end rule, the continuation after the sponsor's retirement or death, and the recertification interval are the terms of the product's eligibility continuation reference and registration requirements schedule.

## Two ways a registration ends

**A. End for loss of eligibility.** The registration ends when DEERS or the case manager shows the beneficiary no longer eligible: the sponsor separated or retired, the qualifying condition no longer present at recertification, or the end of the transitional survivor period. The registration then shows as closed for loss of eligibility, and its end date is the last day of eligibility.

**B. End at the family's request.** The sponsor or the beneficiary's guardian may end a registered ECHO registration at any time. The request is recorded as an intake, and it is the family's own confirmation that ends it. The registration then shows as closed at the family's request, and its end date is the last day of the registration.

## Summary of events

| Event | Ends the registration |
|---|---|
| DEERS shows the sponsor separated | yes |
| DEERS shows the sponsor retired | yes, after the continuation months after retirement |
| The transitional survivor period ends | yes |
| The case manager finds the qualifying condition no longer present at recertification | yes |
| The family's own confirmation, recorded on an intake | yes |

## After the end date

Services after the end date are not paid.

*Hypothetical case, for illustration only:* a registration's end date is the last day of a month; a service on that last day falls on the end date, and a service on the first day of the next month is after the end date and is not paid.
